title: Panasonic Toaster Oven Sold at Costco and Amazon Recalled Over Shock and Fire Risk

body:
Panasonic has issued a recall for its Model No. NB-G200 Electric Toaster Oven across the United States and Canada after determining that the appliance poses a risk of electric shock and fire. Shoppers who purchased the toaster oven at Costco, on Amazon, or through other retailers are urged to stop using it immediately.

What's Being Recalled

The recall covers approximately 11,480 units sold in the US and 2,184 in Canada. According to Panasonic, the power cord insulation "can be insufficient due to a protective fiberglass sleeve not covering it adequately, posing a risk of shock and/or fire hazard." The toaster oven was sold between October 2024 and April 2026 at approximately $170.

Reports Filed So Far

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has received four reports of the toaster oven tripping circuit breakers or outlets. A fifth report noted the appliance stopped working. No injuries have been reported.

What To Do

Both the CPSC and Health Canada urge consumers to stop using the recalled toaster oven and contact Panasonic for a full refund. Costco members can also return the product to any warehouse. This recall adds to a growing list of kitchen appliance safety actions in 2026, including recalled sauté pans, space heaters, and electric kettles previously sold at major retailers.
